body.opens: One index answers every head the store has had: each entry stamped with its act's number, a read as of a head taking the newest entry stamped at or before it, the runs merged by size so they stay about log2 of the entries. The index grows with what changes, never with how many heads there are. Measured on the main store: 26 s and 133 MB where it was 5 min 54 s and 853 MB; a history index reads 1.01 entries per question against a snapshot's.

name: The index stamped with its acts

body.opens: Strata keeps an act as its part, the holons this store keeps as canonical lines with no prev, the same bytes in any store, so the engine hashes every store's part into one content hash; its commit, the act whole with every store's part by the id of its root, its own, its predecessors and number, its name its history hash; its run, stamped with its number; and the head, naming the commit and the runs. Conflicts are read from the runs, the version chain from the stamped ids entries, and gone is taken from every store that keeps it. Measured, facts are diffed against the version before, not stamped by version, which wrote 1.6 times the entries and read large sets 3 to 5 times slower.
restsOn: The part's bytes a contract every kind of store shares, taken as leaned
A store named in parts by the id of its root, taken as leaned
by, and predecessors as a list, taken as leaned
Every store's part written before any head moves, taken as leaned and not yet built
A snapshot-only copy keeping parts under their names, taken as leaned and not yet built
JSON for parts and commits, binary for runs, taken as leaned

name: One act, one commit, kept whole in strata

body.opens: Runs laid as trees of 4 KB pages, read in place one page per level, and blobs kept open so a read is one call to the system: strata holds no data of its own, and the system's page cache does the caching. Measured, reads were the same with strata's cache and without it; 2,000 holons by id 0.3 s, all holons in 84 µs each.

name: The format carries the speed, not caches

body.opens: A panel of agents weighs a decision best when each is given everything, the sessions, Knowledge, the code and what was measured, and left free to explore and disagree, not cast to one narrow angle, which only limits it to the session's own inference. Four free panellists found independently what the cast panels had not: they showed real a hazard a cast panellist had raised and the session had set aside, two writers racing leaving a wrong address in the index, and found two bugs no one had seen.

name: Panels given everything and left free

body.opens: In the browser each blob is kept open through a synchronous handle opened read-only, the browser's descriptor, and a pool of 4 KB pages in memory, storage/pool.ts, wraps any storage and stands in for the page cache the browser does not keep: the decoupled paging piece the author called a Web3 gem. Measured in Chromium, reads at about twice the machine's time with the pool and ten times without.
restsOn: The pool's budget, fixed at 64 MB or following what the device can spare
Read-only handles in Safari and Firefox, unchecked

name: The browser's page pool, its own module

body.opens: The site's build converts each store into strata and writes its head and every blob the head reaches gzipped to strata/<name>/; the browser unpacks each blob with DecompressionStream before checking it against its name. What a read waits on is fetched at once; with whole, the rest is kept behind it, the index first. Main is 12.4 MB over the wire where it was 119.8, unpacked in a third of a second.
restsOn: How the site is hosted and published, the author's to choose

body.opens: An offer writing only history, its part, its commit and the head, and the index caught up by whoever next needs it in one pass over the commits in order, each commit's changes stamped with its number: a conversion, a bulk import and many acts at once then pay for the index only when something reads. Measured: a rebuild from history matches the live index byte for byte, and would take a conversion from about 30 s to about 20.
restsOn: A read that may have to write, to catch the index up

name: The index trailing the commits, as the consumer chooses

body.opens: A published store fetched a page at a time by HTTP range requests, so the present is read with less than the whole: about 78% of the main store, or 62% with a run of the present alone.
restsOn: A hash for each page, since a page cannot be checked against its blob's
Compression lost, a range being counted in compressed bytes

name: A store loaded lazily by pages
